Subject: Fwd: AcmeCloud - AWS marketplace pricing ask (needs escalation)

Marissa / Rafael — forwarding the thread with AcmeCloud. Theyre requesting an unusually large effective discount on the AWS Marketplace listing so they can enable an AWS co-sell motion. Initial numbers: list price + an extra 45% off via promotional code. Procurement is pushing hard and sales can't close without being competitive on marketplace price.

Quick context: AcmeCloud is a large regional systems integrator with a committed pilot for 250 developer seats (anticipated ARR $450k annualized), but their procurement insists the offer be visible in the AWS Marketplace with a promotional discount to qualify for the AWS co-sell program. That discount would exceed our standard marketplace allowance (we usually cap at 25% for co-sell enablement).

Can we get this routed to Deal Desk for formal review? They need to be live in marketplace by end of April to match the partner co-sell schedule. I attach the customer's request and prior term sheet.

Attachments: AcmeCloud_MOP_discount_request.pdf

Thanks,
Rishi

Subject: ESCALATION: AWS Marketplace offer - AcmeCloud request (45% promotional)

Team — escalating per Rishi. Summary and ask below: 

- Customer: AcmeCloud (prospect -> pilot committed)
- Opportunity: 250 seats, estimated first-year ARR $450k, TCV expected $1.2M over 3 years if pilot converts
- Marketplace requirement: Offer must appear in AWS Marketplace with a promo that results in ~45% off list for initial purchase to satisfy partner procurement and co-sell eligibility
- Redwood policy: standard marketplace max promo for co-sell = 25%
- Time sensitivity: AWS co-sell kickoff scheduled week of 4/19; partner is unwilling to proceed without marketplace presence and promotional pricing in place

Questions for Deal Desk:
1) Acceptable governance path to approve >25% promotional discount for marketplace listing?
2) Are there carve-outs (e.g., one-time limited promotional code, short-duration offer) that can be approved administratively vs Board-level?
3) Required offsets (marketing fund, MDF, or co-term commit) to preserve unit economics?

Requested: provisional approval for a 45% promotional discount for a 90-day marketplace window, conditional on (a) customer signs a 12-month contract outside marketplace at list price, or (b) Redwood receives a co-funded marketing commitment from AcmeCloud (suggested minimum $25k).

Attachments: AWS_co-sell_term_sheet_v3.docx, AcmeCloud_MOP_discount_request.pdf

Please advise next steps and required materials. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the details.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all — thanks for the clear write-up. A few items from Deal Desk to help evaluate: 

1) Please provide expected gross margin at list price and at 45% effective discount (include token inference unit economics if possible).
2) Confirm whether AcmeCloud will sign a separate MSA for services/enablement (non-marketplace) with the full list price. If yes, attach the draft.
3) Confirm whether AWS or AcmeCloud will co-fund any portion of the promotion (MDF/marketing).
4) Legal: need confirmation from AcmeCloud Legal that marketplace T&Cs plus our standard SOWs are acceptable; if they require marketplace-only terms we may need additional approvals.

Governance note: discounts >40% require VP Sales + CFO signoff per pricing policy; anything >20% for marketplace co-sell needs a written mitigation plan (MDF, co-term, or reserved capacity).

For expediency, we can provisionally approve a short, one-time promotional code up to 35% for a 30-day window while we collect the required documents. Anything beyond that will be escalated to VP Sales (Rafael) and Finance (Priyom).

Please attach the financial model and customer acceptance language; we'll attempt to fast-track.

Deal Desk

> For expediency, we can provisionally approve a short, one-time promotional code up to 35% for a 30-day window while we collect the required documents. Anything beyond that will be escalated to VP Sales (Rafael) and Finance (Priyom).

Team — after reviewing the numbers Priyom and I discussed offline, heres the decision and conditions: 

Decision: APPROVE a 40% promotional discount on the AWS Marketplace offer, limited to a single-use promotional code applied to the pilot purchase. This is an exception to the standard 25% cap and requires the following mandatory conditions: 

1) Customer signs a separate 12-month contract at list price for ongoing seats and professional services within 14 days of pilot activation. Document must be countersigned by both parties.
2) AcmeCloud commits to co-funded partner marketing (MDF) of at least $25k credited against Redwood marketing activities; evidence of funds must be received before marketplace publish.
3) Promotion window limited to 60 days from publish date; code is single-use and tied to the AcmeCloud account.
4) Legal to add a short addendum stating Redwood can reclaim promotional credit if customer churns before 90 days.
5) Finance to track the pilot as a non-recurring promotional deduction and report actual margin impact in monthly revenue review.

Rationale: the strategic value of enabling AWS co-sell with AcmeCloud (channel expansion + potential $1.2M TCV) justifies a one-time deeper promotion, provided we secure the mitigations above.

Next steps: Marissa/Rishi — please coordinate with AcmeCloud and AWS rep (Erin Walsh) to capture the signatures/MDF commitment and kick off legal addendum. Priyom, Lauren — please confirm finance/legal checklist and turn-around expectations.

Thanks,
Rafael
